transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-01-15
Start time: 10:00 AM PST
Duration: ~72 minutes
Location: Zoom (all-hands)
Attendees: Sam Patel, Maria Lopez, Jordan Kim, Liam O'Connor, Avery Chen + All staff (virtual)

Summary:
Company all-hands covering Q1 priorities, product roadmap highlights (Dedicated / Private / Optimize), hiring profile, security updates, and revenue motion. Short Q&A and closing remarks.

Topics:
- Business metrics & ARR cadence
- Product roadmap: Dedicated autoscaling, Private on-prem package, Optimize recommendations engine
- Reliability and incident postmortem highlights
- Security: SOC 2, KMS/HSM, audit logs
- Go-to-market: PLG motions, enterprise playbook, renewals
- Hiring and org updates

Action items (as called out in meeting):
- See metadata action_items for owners and due dates.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sam Patel: hey everyone, good morning, uh, thanks for joining the january all-hands. i'm Sam, uh, a couple of quick house-keeping notes before we jump in. we'll run about an hour, 65 to 75 minutes, recording is on, slides will be shared after.

[00:20] Crowd noise / applause / Sam: alright let's get started. first slide-- quick state of the company. 

[00:35] Sam Patel: 2025 closed strong, we hit our ARR target, we grew 48% year-over-year, and Q4 got a lot of the momentum from Dedicated signups, so thanks to Revenue and Product for the heavy lift there. we are projecting a conservative start to Q1 but the funnel is healthy. Liam do you want to add quick color?

[00:55] Liam O'Connor: yeah thanks Sam. pipeline is up 30% q-o-q, top of funnel is broad—self-serve is healthy—couple of big enterprise deals in late stage. churn is stable. main focus for rev org in Q1 is scaling renewals and land-and-expand for our top 20 accounts. we'll share a renewal playbook targeted at those accounts by end of month.

[01:20] Sam Patel: awesome, thank you. okay product, Jordan?

[01:25] Jordan Kim: sure. quick note—our roadmap for Q1 centers on three things: 1) Dedicated autoscaling and burst capacity GA, 2) Private on-prem packaging for regulated customers, and 3) Redwood Optimize, which is the recommendations engine for batching/quantization suggestions.

[01:45] Jordan Kim: for Dedicated autoscale—this is the feature customers have been asking for to get reserved throughput but still handle spikes. we did a closed beta with two customers and saw 20-35% reduction in cost per request when combined with prefix caching. we'll start broad beta next week.

[02:05] Maria Lopez: and from an infra perspective we've been tuning the serving runtime—kernel selection improvements dropped P90 latency by about 12% for the long-sequence workloads; fingers crossed once autoscale is in GA that latency SLOs will be easier to maintain under load. there's still some work around KV cache eviction policies.

[02:30] Speaker 1 (someone off mic): hey quick question, is the KV cache change backwards compatible with current model variants?

[02:35] Jordan Kim: yeah it's compatible; it's config-side only, so customers won't have to redeploy models, but we'll be sure to include migration notes.

[02:45] Sam Patel: thanks. security update—Avery or Maria?

[02:50] Maria Lopez: Avery will lead this.

[02:52] Avery Chen: hi all. short update: SOC 2 readiness is on track, audit kick-off next month. we're also rolling out KMS integrations for both hosted and Private customers—HSM support is in the backlog but prioritized for Q2. audit logs and retention policies now have a clear path; we'll publish a roadmap with timelines by 1/29. quick note: customers in regulated industries asked about data residency—Private deployments now have a simplified template for Europe region installs.

[03:25] [crosstalk / someone laughs] Speaker 2: that's great—when's the after party?

[03:30] Sam Patel: no after party this time. ok engineering hiring update, Maria?

[03:34] Maria Lopez: hiring is ramping—we've opened 18 roles across infra and runtime, primarily in the US and Lisbon. goal is to reduce bus factor on critical kernels and to finish the autoscale integration. also investing in SRE headcount to reduce toil. note: interview loops will change slightly—we're adding a runtime design round for infra-facing candidates.

[03:55] Sam Patel: thanks. product-market fit and go-to-market—Jordan?

[04:00] Jordan Kim: two experiments for PLG this quarter: 1) new quickstart templates for embedding-based search use cases, 2) a 'pay-as-you-grow' Dedicated demo that lets teams simulate burst traffic. We're also codifying a set of 'quality gates' to prevent model regressions in production—if a model fails a quality eval, it can't be rolled out without a remediation plan.

[04:30] Jordan Kim: note on competitors—we're watching Anthropic's model updates and OpenAI's pricing moves; both impact positioning. our differentiation continues to be predictable economics and deployment flexibility.

[04:50] Liam O'Connor: also, marketing will run a cohort play focused on mid-market PLG accounts to drive MQLs for Dedicated; should help funnel into the renewal motion later.

[05:05] Sam Patel: okay quick operational highlights—incident review from december. Maria?

[05:10] Maria Lopez: december 14th incident was due to a misconfigured autoscaler policy in a Directed Dedicated pool, causing cascading capacity reclaim; full post-mortem is published on confluence. key fixes: safer defaults, better validation in the control plane, and a circuit-breaker to prevent global reclaim when one pool spikes. expected to reduce recurrence risk significantly.

[05:35] Sam Patel: good. people updates—promotions, shoutouts.

[05:40] Sam Patel: shoutout to the infra team—onboarding the Dedicated beta customers was messy but they did really well. promotions: Elena to Staff SRE, Anil to Principal ML Engineer. Congratulations.

[06:00] [brief applause / emoji reaction in chat]

[06:10] Q&A opens up. Attendee question: customer support SLA improvements?

[06:15] Liam O'Connor: support SLA—we're rolling out tiered SLAs for dedicated customers, with faster response and a dedicated technical advisor for enterprise. we'll also pilot a premium observability add-on for top accounts.

[06:35] Attendee: what's the plan for on-prem installs for air-gapped environments?

[06:40] Avery Chen: short answer: it's available but requires enterprise licensing. long answer: we have a packaged on-prem installer and a private control plane option; the team will work with security to validate KMS and network isolation. we expect a formal on-prem GA by late Q1 for a limited set of partners.

[07:05] Attendee (voice blurred): any updates on model catalog curation and redwood-verified profiles?

[07:10] Jordan Kim: yes—redwood-verified performance profiles are expanding. we added three new LLM variants in the catalog with quantization profiles tested on A100 and H100 hardware. note: some of the auto-labeling in the catalog UI has noisy names—working on a fix; apologies for the churn.

[07:35] Sam Patel: ok, a couple forward-looking things. small teams: please align your team OKRs to the company-level cost and reliability targets. 2 big measurable goals for the company in Q1: reduce per-token unit cost by 8% via batching/caching/quantization improvements, and hit 99.9% uptime across Dedicated pools.

[08:05] Maria Lopez: to add, the runtime team is experimenting with a new attention kernel that has promising perf on longer sequences; if the benchmarks hold, it will be a big lever for cost.

[08:20] [Silence, typing in chat] Speaker 3: can we get a summary email after?

[08:25] Sam Patel: yes Avery will send recording + slides + highlights.

[08:30] Quick lightning round from each functional leader (30–45 seconds each):
[08:32] Maria Lopez: infra—focus on autoscale, KV cache eviction fixes, hiring.

[08:45] Jordan Kim: product—Dedicated GA planning, Private packaging, Optimize recommender rollout, catalog fixes.

[08:55] Liam O'Connor: GTM—renewal playbook, enterprise pilot, marketing cohort for PLG.

[09:05] Avery Chen: devrel & docs—improve quickstarts, publish SOC 2 timeline, share on-prem install checklist.

[09:20] Sam Patel: final thoughts—thanks everyone, big push this quarter, focus on predictability and reliability for customers. we'll do a mid-quarter update.

[09:35] Closing: Sam: ok that's it. recording will be posted, please fill out the short pulse survey in Slack. see you all in standups.

[09:45] End recording.

Notes on transcription: occasional name mis-recognition ("Redwoods" vs "Redwood"), filler words kept, minor timestamps approximate.
